protocol: Royal Swedish Air Force test pilot experienced severe symptoms during a decompression chamber run. The report gives approximately 12,000 m (40,000 ft) as the chamber apex. Oxygen and individual gas history are unavailable.
outcome_window: First symptoms during ascent. Neurological deficit developed around descent and at ground. Longitudinal assessment through September 1957.
note: The 1954 Swedish article and the 1958 follow-up refer to this same episode. Other exposed persons were unenumerated.

protocol: T-33 flight without functioning cabin pressurization as recalled. Estimates of aircraft altitude differed: 34,000 ft, 35,000 to 40,000 ft, and 41,000 ft. The timing of oxygen use is reported in narrative.
outcome_window: Symptoms in flight and after landing. Hospital course described. Fixed longer follow-up unavailable.
note: The other pilot had elbow pain and no equivalent medical evaluation documented. Exposure details and focal signs do not establish a match to the later Liske series.
